## Personality

Bold, restless and fond of a grand gesture. She never turns down a dare and rarely turns down a contract.

## Lore

Seraphine is the captain of the Bright Morrow, the fastest trading ship in Bain Harbour, and she would like you to know it. She is thirty-six, bold, restless and fond of a grand gesture. She never turns down a dare and rarely turns down a contract, and she brings the Bright Morrow into harbour under more sail than anyone thinks wise, swinging up to the pier with a flourish that makes the dockworkers duck and Garrow the foreman swear.

### The fastest ship in the harbour

Seraphine went to sea at fourteen as a ship's girl on a coasting trader, and she spent the next thirteen years climbing from the rigging to the quarterdeck on other people's ships, impatient at every step. At twenty-seven she bought the Bright Morrow from a merchant who was giving up the sea. She was old and slow then, and everyone on the Waterfront told Seraphine she had paid too much. Seraphine rebuilt her rig with taller masts and more canvas, scraped her hull clean, and within a year the Bright Morrow was beating every ship in the harbour from the headland to the pier. That was nine years ago. She has not been beaten since, and she has never let anyone forget it.

She carries spices, cloth and anything that needs to arrive quickly, and merchants pay her a premium for speed the way they pay Captain Corwin of the Heron a premium for care. Seraphine and Corwin are opposites and both enjoy it. She likes to remind him, loudly and at the council's door, that the Heron is the second fastest ship in the harbour at best. He likes to remind her, quietly, that he has never lost a crate. Ysolde, the Keeper of the Light, tells her every chance she gets that she comes in far too fast and will one day meet the harbour wall. Seraphine blows her a kiss from the deck.

### What she saw

Seraphine has sailed more deep-water voyages than any other captain in the harbour, because the fastest routes run furthest out, and she has seen more of the new creatures in the deep water than anyone. She will not describe what she saw. Asked about it at the Salt and Bread, she laughs and changes the subject, and if pressed she buys the whole table a drink, which is a grand gesture and also a very effective way of ending a conversation.

What she does instead is pay. Since that voyage she has sailed with hired adventurers on every trip, more of them than any other captain, and she pays them better than anyone on the waterfront. Her current favourite is Keziah, a sword for hire from inland who counts the exits in every room and has a dry wit Seraphine enjoys. Seraphine has asked Keziah to sign on for the whole summer, and she does not understand why such a cool head always looks so grey at sea.

Her bosun, Barnaby, has sailed with her since the day she bought the ship. He is big, loud and soft-hearted, and his stories are famous for being exaggerated. When he came back from the night watch last autumn and told the Waterfront about a pair of eyes as large as cartwheels looking up at him from under the hull, everyone laughed. Seraphine did not. She listened to the end, went to her cabin, and shut the door. She has never told him why.

### What she wants and fears

Seraphine wants to be the first ship to sail somewhere no Bain Harbour ship has been, and she keeps a blank sheet of chart paper rolled in her cabin, for waters past the edge of anything Ambrose the chartmaker has drawn, on which she means to draw the first line herself. She fears nothing she will name. But she has stopped taking dares that involve the deep water at night.

### Hooks

A quest could sign on as one of Seraphine's hired adventurers, take her up on a dare she cannot refuse, or find out what she saw from her deck, which she has told no one at all.
